Chemical stoichiometry 
When substances react to give a chemical compound, their proportions 
are fixed in a stoichiometric ratio, which is also known as the mole ratio of 
an eqguation. This ratio is shown by the stoichiometric coefficients before the 
species in the equation. An equation with correct stoichiometric coefficients is 
said to be balanced, which means that there is the same number of each type 
of atom on each side.

Theoretical, experimental and percentage yield 
The expected amount, mass or volume of areaction product is known 
as the theoretical yield of that product. The theoretical yield is rarely 
obtained in practice because of side reactions and losses of products 
during their separation and purification. 
The actual quantity of a product isolated from the reaction mixture is 
known as the experimental yield of that product. 
The percentage yield is calculated as follows: 
experimental yield % vyield = x 100% theoretical yield

Atom economy and green chemistry 
Atom economy is an important concept of green chemistry and a measure of 
the efficiency of a chemical or industrial process. It is calculated as follows: 
mass of desired products(s) % 100% % atom economy = total mass of reactants 
For example, the addition polymerization (Structure 2.4) of propene has an 
atom economy of 100%, as all atoms from the reactant (propene) end up in the 
reaction product (polypropene): 
catalyst nCH3;—CH=—7CH; ———— CH—CH; heat 
CHj n 
In contrast, the atom economy of a condensation polymerization (Structure 2.4 
AHL) is always less than T00% because some of the atoms from the reactants 
end up in the reaction by-product. 
Green chemistry is an approach to chemical research and engineering 
that seeks to minimize the production and release to the environment of 
hazardous substances. Common practices of green chemistry include 
atom economy and the use of agueous or solvent-free reactions, 
renewable starting materials, mild reaction conditions, energy-saving 
techniques, efficient catalysts and utilization of by-products. The high cost 
of some “green” technologies is compensated by lower spending on 
environmental remediation, waste management and energy.
